title: One shared drag slot has no gesture ownership — a touch press or pad A can hijack (or commit) an in-progress mouse drag
detail: All three devices share ONE drag state and begin_draw overwrites it unconditionally. A finger tap mid-mouse-drag re-anchors the drag at the touch node; pad A commits whatever drag is active. dispatch_frame orders devices deterministically, but no device owns the gesture, so concurrent dual-device use corrupts gestures. T1 drives one device per run, so this path is untested.
recommended_fix: Add a gesture-owner field (the device that began the drag); gate Begin_Draw/Confirm/retarget/commit on ownership, and add a mixed-device-frame T1 scenario.

title: mouse_map allocates + frees a heap dynamic every frame — per-frame heap churn in the input hot path
detail: poll_mouse emits a Mouse_Move every frame unconditionally, so mouse_map allocates the moves buffer and frees it each frame (poll.odin appends the per-frame pos read every frame). Violates the project rule 'zero per-frame heap churn (frame arena)'. events/intents avoid this by persisting on Input; moves is the only per-frame dynamic.
recommended_fix: Persist the moves buffer on Input (clear() per frame like events/intents), or use a fixed-size stack array for the frame's move positions.

title: Effect hooks pass an untyped rawptr user — the one untyped seam in an otherwise strongly typed layer, and a departure from the events-not-callbacks convention
evidence:
input.odin:70-71: "user:            rawptr,
	on_retry:        proc(user: rawptr, inp: ^Input),          // fresh run (E32)"
main.odin:559: "app := cast(^App)user"
detail: Eleven app-effect proc hooks + a rawptr user form the app<->input contract; every effect casts (project-context: 'Events, not callbacks... No function-pointer webs' ODN-14). A miscast user compiles clean and corrupts at runtime. Pragmatic for cycle avoidance (input cannot import package main), but a future caller has no compile-time guard.
recommended_fix: Keep the hooks but wrap user in a typed context struct wired once in main (as now); document the cast invariant, or drain executor-produced effect events via the app's existing per-tick event pattern.

title: The 'input' package now hosts QoS business rules and selection/demolish command production — UI (qos_panel) depends on it
evidence:
exec.odin:457: "qos_mode_manual :: proc(inp: ^Input, ps: u32) -> bool {"
exec.odin:474: "qos_apply_auto :: proc(inp: ^Input, pipe: u32) {"
exec.odin:497: "set_lane_class :: proc(inp: ^Input, class: u16, lane: u8) {"
qos_panel.odin:5: "import inp \"./input\" // 5.4: the shared executor's lane/QoS command producers"
detail: The lane/QoS auto-follow ladder and lane assignment moved from qos_panel into exec.odin, so the QoS panel (UI) now calls into the input package to produce commands. Dependency direction is acyclic and the move is structurally motivated (harness cannot import package main), but the package's scope now spans input mapping, world hit-testing, selection UX, and QoS domain logic.
recommended_fix: Document the package as the shared command-executor layer (its header already says 'ONE shared executor'), and if it grows, split the executor + command producers into their own package both input and qos_panel import.
